title: The 8 Best Table Saw Blades 2026
metaDescription: Our 8 picks for table saw blades 2026, with key specs, strengths and limitations for each, based on manufacturer specs, independent reviews and owner reports.
lede: We looked at table saw blades 2026 using manufacturer specs, independent reviews and owner reports. Each pick lists what it does well and where it falls short, so you can match it to how you'll use it.

products.name: Freud LU83R010 10-Inch 50-Tooth Combination Blade
products.blurb: Key specs: 50-tooth ATB+R, 10-inch diameter, Freud carbide.
strengths: 50-tooth ATB+R geometry handles both ripping and crosscutting adequately from one blade
Freud carbide is the sharpest and most consistent of anybrand
Anti-vibration slots reduce blade resonance and body heat buildup
The most commonly recommended all-around table saw blade by furniture woodworkers
limitations: A combination blade compromises -- a dedicated rip blade rips faster, a dedicated crosscut blade is cleaner
Not the correct blade for production ripping or very fine miter work
products.bestFor: buyers who want the best overall package

products.name: Freud LM72R010 10-Inch 24-Tooth Heavy-Duty Rip Blade
products.blurb: Key specs: 24-tooth flat top grind, For ripping, Aggressive material removal.
strengths: 24 FTG teeth cut along the grain aggressively for fast, smooth rip cuts
Flat top grind produces a flat-bottomed kerf -- correct for dado applications and tenon cheeks
The fastest rip cut of anyblade -- significantly faster than combination blades
The correct dedicated rip blade for production ripping and furniture parts
limitations: Not for crosscutting -- 24 FTG teeth produce tearout on cross-grain cuts

products.name: Freud LU80R010 10-Inch 80-Tooth Ultimate Plywood & Melamine Blade
products.blurb: Key specs: 80-tooth ATB, Fine crosscut, Plywood and hardwood.
strengths: 80 ATB teeth produce the cleanest crosscut surface of anyblade -- near zero tearout
The correct blade for crosscutting solid hardwood to final length for furniture parts
Also the correct blade for cutting plywood to finished size without tearout
Freud carbide quality produces a finish-ready surface that requires no sanding on most species
limitations: 80 teeth is too many for ripping -- generates excessive heat in the kerf during rip cuts
Slower feed rate required than combination blades

products.name: Diablo D1040X 10-Inch 40-Tooth General Purpose Blade
products.blurb: Key specs: 40-tooth ATB, Diablo carbide, General purpose.
strengths: Diablo (Freud's value brand) carbide quality at a significantly lower price than Freud
40-tooth ATB handles general furniture ripping and crosscutting
The most commonly sold table saw blade at home improvement stores
The correct blade when budget matters and general work quality is the goal
limitations: 40 teeth is a compromise -- fewer teeth than an 80-tooth crosscut, more than a 24-tooth rip
Slightly lower carbide quality than Freud blades
products.bestFor: value-focused buyers who want the most for their money

products.name: Forrest WW10407125 Woodworker II 10-Inch 40-Tooth Blade
products.blurb: Key specs: 40-tooth ATBR, Hand-tensioned, New Jersey made.
strengths: Hand-tensioned blade body -- the most precise plate flatness of anyblade
New Jersey manufactured -- the last major American saw blade manufacturer
ATBR tooth geometry handles both ripping and crosscutting with exceptional surface quality
Resharpenable through Forrest's sharpening service -- a lifetime blade investment
limitations: Long lead time when ordering directly from Forrest
products.bestFor: buyers who want the best overall package

products.name: Freud LU98R010 10-Inch 80-Tooth Single-Sided Laminate/Melamine Blade
products.blurb: Key specs: 80 teeth, Plywood and veneer, TCG grind.
strengths: TCG (triple chip grind) tooth geometry designed for composite materials, plywood, and veneer
Minimal tearout on plywood faces -- the primary challenge when cutting plywood panels
The correct blade for cabinet shops and furniture makers who cut large quantities of plywood
Can also crosscut solid wood cleanly
limitations: Higher price than the 80-tooth ATB for slightly different geometry

products.name: CMT 215.050.10 Industrial Combination Blade 10-Inch 50-Tooth
products.blurb: Key specs: 50-tooth ATB, Italian carbide, Non-stick coating.
strengths: Italian carbide quality -- CMT uses the same carbide grade as Freud
Non-stick coating prevents resin buildup during cutting
50-tooth ATB combination geometry for both rip and crosscut
The European professional standard for Italian and European furniture shop blades
limitations: Less commonly available at retail than Freud or Diablo
Higher price than Diablo for similar performance

products.name: Irwin Tools 1807370 Marples 10-Inch 80-Tooth Circular Saw Blade
products.blurb: Key specs: 80-tooth ATB, Fine crosscut, Marples quality.
strengths: 80-tooth ATB fine crosscut at a lower price than Freud 80-tooth
Laser-cut body for consistent plate flatness
Marples is the premium Irwin quality brand
The correct value alternative to the Freud 80-tooth for crosscutting furniture parts
limitations: Slightly lower carbide quality than Freud over many sharpenings
products.bestFor: value-focused buyers who want the most for their money

howWeChose: Picks are based on manufacturer specs, independent reviews and owner reports. We don't claim our own testing.
